0.long_answer: Acromegaly is most commonly caused by a benign tumor of the anterior pituitary gland known as a pituitary adenoma. This non-metastasizing tumor, particularly a somatotroph adenoma, produces excess growth hormone, leading to the characteristic symptoms of acromegaly. Although the tumor is benign and does not metastasize, its hormone secretion causes systemic effects and can lead to various complications if left untreated.
